title: SOC2 scope sketch — user-side checklist and evidence notes
content:
Quick scratchpad: top-of-head notes for scoping SOC2 readiness — not polished. Purpose: capture scope decisions, obvious evidence, open questions to surface in Wed sync with infra/product.

Scope assumptions (working):
- Primary in-scope services: Redwood API (hosted), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem package) — focus on data-in-scope paths for customer-facing inference endpoints and control-plane components that manage keys/rollouts.
- Exclude non-prod demo tenants unless they share production secrets or tokens. Include staging if it exercises same CI/CD and secrets.
- Include Console (observability + rollouts) because it has token-level traces and role-based access.

Inventory (quick list of systems to map to controls):
- API frontend (hosted-api): ingress LB, auth (API keys, internal token service), rate limit config.
- Serving runtime clusters: dedicated pools + private install packages (onprem manifests).
- Control plane: deployment orchestrator, model catalog, rollout engine.
- Console & observability: dashboards, tracing, & audit logs retention store (ELK/observability cluster).
- IAM/SSO: Okta + SCIM provisioning, admin role sets.
- Secrets/KMS: cloud KMS for hosted, HSM option for private — note where customer keys are stored.
- CI/CD: release-engineering pipelines, feature flags (rollouts), PR approvals.
- On-call / incident: paging, runbooks in ops playbooks, postmortem backlog.

Control mapping notes + candidate evidence (brain dump):
- Logical access (AC):
  - Evidence: Okta group membership export, SCIM provisioning logs, admin access lists, recent user access reviews (quarterly emails), SSO SAML metadata.
  - Tickets: JIRA-SEC-110 (okta scim fixes), github.com/redwood-inference/enterprise/patch-312 (scim sync PR).
  - Owner: Asha Gupta (infra identity).

- Change management (CC):
  - Evidence: Git history for infra repos (protected branches), signed PR approvals, release notes, deploy runbook IDs, canary deploy history from console.
  - Artifacts: CICD job logs, PR IDs for major releases, policy doc for emergency change process.
  - Owner: Liam Park (release-eng).

- System operations / availability (SRE):
  - Evidence: SLO dashboards, pagerduty escalation policies, runbooks, incident postmortems for last 12 months.
  - Things to collect: evidence that autoscaling and fallback policies work (load tests + demo runbook).
  - Owner: SRE (TBD) — ask Jamie for runbook bundle.

- Logging & monitoring (Detection):
  - Evidence: audit logs retention config, sample log exports (anonymized), index lifecycle policies, ACLs on log storage.
  - Note: ensure token-level traces are scrubbed or redacted in evidence artifacts.

- Encryption (in transit & at rest):
  - Evidence: TLS cert configs (LB, internal mTLS), KMS key listings, key rotation records, HSM attestation docs for private installs.
  - Question: do Dedicated customers provide their own KMS keys? Need to capture both hosted and dedicated flows.

- Vendor / third-party & datacenter controls:
  - Evidence: cloud provider contracts, SOC2/HIPAA certs from our cloud vendor (if used), vendor risk assessments.

Open questions / risks (to resolve in sync):
- Scope boundary for Dedicated: customer isolation — does resource-level separation reduce evidence requirements? Practically, we still operate control plane that can interact with pools.
- Private (on-prem) evidence: customers install in their environment — we can only provide packaging and docs; need a checklist for what vendor evidence customers must supply for their install. Draft a customer-provided-evidence template.
- Retention windows: product currently defaults to 30 days for traces; need to show policy for audit logs retention >= 1 year? Confirm with Observability team.
- Admin user access reviews: do we have a recurring recorded process? If not, implement a quarterly calendar invite + export.
- Model rollout approval steps: how to demonstrate approval? Add signed approvals or PRs that gated model changes.

Immediate TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- Create master control mapping sheet (Confluence + links to artifacts). Assign to me (Sofia) to stub initial mapping.
- Pull Okta group membership export and store in evidence bucket (JIRA-INFRA-324).
- Ask Asha for KMS key rotation history — make sure to redact key material in evidence.
- Draft customer-evidence checklist for Private installs (target: single page PDF they can fill).
- Request retention policy export from observability (Liam to coordinate).

Meeting agenda for Wed sync (30m):
1) Confirm scope (5m) — which environments explicitly in/out.
2) Owner assignments (5m) — who owns each control group.
3) Evidence gaps (10m) — top 5 hardest items and blockers.
4) Next steps + deadlines (10m).

Notes on evidence hygiene / redaction:
- Never upload raw keys or full token dumps. When pulling logs for demonstration, mask tokens and PII (use grep/sed pipeline). Keep redaction steps in each evidence artifact description.
- Produce a short README per evidence item describing: what it is, who pulled it, redaction applied, relevant date range.

Backlog items (later):
- Automate periodic evidence exports (Okta, KMS key rotation, audit logs) into secure evidence bucket with versioning and checksum.
- Small script to generate "redaction-friendly" log exports (remove api_key, auth_token fields).
- Template for control owner sign-off with date and optional supporting links.

Random ideas / brainstorm:
- Lightweight attestation flow for Dedicated customers: they sign an attestation that their dedicated pool config meets our baseline, we collect a minimal telemetry snapshot.
- For Private installs, offer a 'self-attestation package' customers can run that outputs a compliance bundle for us to review.

Quick contact list (to ping):
- Asha Gupta (infra identity)
- Liam Park (release-eng)
- Jamie Chen (SRE lead)
- Priya Desai (observability)

End notes: this is a working scratchpad. Will iteratively move items to Confluence once owners confirm. Keep this file as the earliest scratch notes and brain dump (timestamped).
